description: 1994 is the Year of the Wood Dog in the Chinese zodiac, from February 10, 1994 to January 30, 1995. Personality, Lunar New Year dates and numerology.
answer: In Chinese astrology, 1994 is the Year of the Wood Dog, a Yang year. It began at Lunar New Year on February 10, 1994 and ended on January 30, 1995, so people born in 1994 before Feb 10 belong to the Water Rooster year.

sections.heading: 1994 Lunar New Year: start and end dates
paragraphs: Lunar New Year opened the Wood Dog year on February 10, 1994, and the year ran to January 30, 1995. So a birth date of Feb 10, 1994 or later counts as Wood Dog, and so do early 1995 birthdays through Jan 30; births in 1994 before Feb 10 still belong to the Water Rooster. That moving boundary comes from the lunisolar calendar, in which the new year starts with the second new moon after the winter solstice in most years, so its Gregorian date shifts by up to a month from one year to the next. Look sixty years either side and the pairing repeats: 1934 are Wood Dog years too. That Thursday new year arrived with the Sun in Aquarius in the Western zodiac.

sections.heading: What the Wood Dog is like
paragraphs: In a Wood Dog year, the Dog's protective loyalty extends outwards to communities and causes. Classical readings describe people born now as generous, cooperative and strongly principled. Wood's push against Earth keeps them engaged with the world, though it can also create inner unease. Choosing a few causes to serve deeply, and checking trust before giving it, are the usual suggestions.

In the five-element scheme, Wood belongs to the east and to the green energy of early spring, and that seasonal image shapes how it colours an animal sign. A Wood stem tends to soften sharp edges and add warmth, curiosity and a cooperative instinct. Traditional texts associate it with benevolence, growth and the wish to build something that lasts beyond the self. People born under a Wood stem are often portrayed as principled, open-handed and hopeful about others. The caution usually attached to Wood is a habit of spreading energy thinly, saying yes to every request and feeling quietly hurt when generosity is not returned in kind.

sections.heading: 1994 in the animal cycle and in numerology
paragraphs: In numerology the year reduces to 5, the number of change, freedom and movement, and a 5 year is usually described as restless and full of variety. The digits of 1994 add up to 23, which reduces to 5. The Dog holds the eleventh place among the twelve animals and its fixed element is Earth. Set beside the year's Wood stem, wood controls Earth, which readings use to describe how settled or stretched the combination feels. The year before was the Water Rooster and the year after is the Wood Pig.

Chinese almanacs name 1994 Jia-Xu, pairing the Wood stem Jia with the branch Xu. Both are Yang, as stem and branch always share a polarity, so of the hundred and twenty possible pairings only sixty ever occur, and each one names a single year in every cycle.

faq.question: What Chinese zodiac is 1994?
faq.answer: 1994 is the Year of the Wood Dog. It started on February 10, 1994 and ended on January 30, 1995.

faq.question: What if I was born in January or February 1994?
faq.answer: Check the date against Feb 10. Born before February 10, 1994, you are a Water Rooster; born on or after it, you are a Wood Dog.

faq.question: What element is 1994 in the Chinese zodiac?
faq.answer: Wood, a Yang year. The Dog's own fixed element is Earth; the year element changes every two years, while the fixed element stays with the animal.

faq.question: What is the traditional Chinese name for 1994?
faq.answer: Jia-Xu. The first part is the heavenly stem, which carries the year's element and polarity; the second is the earthly branch, which carries the animal. Almanacs, calendars and Four Pillars charts identify years this way rather than by animal alone.

faq.question: When is the next Wood Dog year?
faq.answer: 2054, sixty years later, when the five elements and twelve animals line up again; the table also has 1934.
